Where the condos are and what to know

items.t: Highway 1 access is at the Prest Road and Annis Road interchanges per the same page.

The ground is planned through the City's Agricultural Area Plan, Schedule B1 of the Chilliwack 2050 Official Community Plan, Bylaw No. 5500 — the city-wide plan. The Sardis neighbourhood plan is Schedule B5 of the same bylaw (never "Schedule D / Bylaw 5024").

Services are outside the area: the nearest City recreation centres are Chilliwack Landing Leisure Centre, Unit 1, 9145 Corbould Street, and Cheam Leisure Centre, 45501 Market Way; the nearest library is Chilliwack Library, 45860 First Avenue; the nearest hospital is Chilliwack General Hospital, 45600 Menholm Rd, Chilliwack; the nearest grocery named by the City is Save-on-Foods, 46020 Yale Road.

Form B (strata law): Strata Property Act s. 59 — on a resale purchase the strata must provide a Form B Information Certificate stating strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and a summary of the strata's insurance, with rules, budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. It has no application to the freehold farm and rural parcels that make up this sub-area.

The school name is older than the board name. East Chilliwack Elementary's own history page records that the East Chilliwack School District was created on April 14, 1890 after a petition to the Government, that settler Chas Brown donated one acre of land for the school, and that the present building replaced the 1949 school in 1993.

A new school may redraw the east side. The Province's capital projects page lists a new SD33 east-side elementary school under construction at 10125 McGrath Road — a three-storey school providing 500 new student spaces for grades K–5, with a neighbourhood learning centre for child care programming, an estimated project value of $58.6 million, and estimated occupancy April 2027 — which may redraw east-side catchments; verify the exact address in the locator close to purchase.

Drainage and dyking are a separate line on the tax bill. Chilliwack levies additional taxes for drainage and dyking on top of the municipal rates — a rural-buyer cost that does not appear in a municipal-rate-only comparison.

The Sardis plan number is a trap for this area too. East Chilliwack is governed by the Agricultural Area Plan, Schedule B1 of OCP Bylaw 5500; documents citing a "Schedule D" plan or Bylaw 5024 for any Chilliwack neighbourhood are citing a plan structure that does not exist in the current bylaw.

Tax-regime statement, up front: East Chilliwack is inside the City of Chilliwack, so the city tax regime applies — 2026 taxes due the first working day after July 1, 5% penalty on taxes outstanding after July 2, 2026 and a further 5% after August 4, 2026. The FVRD rural regime (Taxation (Rural Area) Act s. 11, 5% plus 5%) does not apply to East Chilliwack.
Where the townhomes are and what to know

items.t: Nearby areas: downtown Chilliwack and Little Mountain to the west and northwest, Rosedale to the east, and the Cheam / Fraser River side to the north.

Schools named for the area (Ministry-listed names only): East Chilliwack Elementary (K–5), 49190 Chilliwack Central Road, and Cheam Elementary (K–5), 9895 Banford Road, on the provincial school list; SD33's structure is elementary K–5, middle 6–8 and secondary 9–12.

Where land is in the ALR: generally no more than one residence per parcel; a principal residence built without an ALC application capped at 500 m² total floor area; and one additional detached residence up to 90 m² on parcels of 40 ha or less or 186 m² on larger parcels. BC Assessment farm-classification minimum gross farm income is in full three-tier form — $10,000 (under 0.8 ha), $2,500 (0.8–4 ha), and $2,500 plus 5% of the actual value of the area in excess of 4 ha (over 4 ha); a flat "$2,500+" statement is an error wherever it is met.

blocks.text: Lots and land in East Chilliwack
What trades here

items.t: Fee-simple farm and rural parcels are the only land form: typical types are rural detached houses on half-acre to multi-acre lots, hobby farms, equestrian properties, and commercial dairy, poultry, nursery and forage farms in the ALR; the Agricultural Area Plan says the farm sector in the plan area is dominated by dairy and poultry operations, nurseries and greenhouses. A parcel here is bought whole (title, farm buildings, residence rights as the ALR rules allow), not as a serviced lot in a subdivision product.

Lot sizes/zones: under Zoning Bylaw 2020 No. 5000, the AL zone sets a minimum lot area of 7.5 ha for land excluded or exempted from the ALR or approved for subdivision within the ALR, 1 ha for a boundary adjustment, and 0.2 ha for a homesite severance or boundary adjustment approved by the Agricultural Land Commission; minimum lot width is 25 m. Smaller residential lots exist near the school and along Chilliwack Central Road, but no residential zone minimum for them was confirmed from the bylaw text. No typical lot size beyond the zone minimums is given.

Bare-land strata: none — and barred on ALR ground: Residences in the ALR cannot be stratified without the ALC's permission — depositing a strata plan is a subdivision, and a person must not subdivide agricultural land unless permitted by the Commission or under the ALR General Regulation (ALCA, s. 21(1); ALC Information Bulletin 09, s. 6; Strata Property Act, s. 239).
Strata vs freehold

Flood/diking character of the land: the City's Floodplain Regulation Bylaw 2018, No. 4519 sets minimum building setbacks of 60 m from the Fraser River, 75 m from the Vedder River and 30 m from the Chilliwack River and Vedder Canal, and the City maintains a diking network for the Fraser and Vedder systems; Chilliwack also levies additional taxes for drainage and dyking on top of the municipal rates.

blocks.text: Where lots come up and what to know

items.t: Planning frame: the ground is planned through the City's Agricultural Area Plan, Schedule B1 of the Chilliwack 2050 Official Community Plan, Bylaw 2025, No. 5500 (Chilliwack 2050). For reference so the schedules are never confused: Sardis = Schedule B5 and Eastern Hillsides = Schedule B4 of the same bylaw.

Schools physically in or named for the area (Ministry-listed names only): East Chilliwack Elementary (K–5), 49190 Chilliwack Central Road, and Cheam Elementary (K–5), 9895 Banford Road. SD33's structure is elementary K–5, middle 6–8 and secondary 9–12. A new SD33 east-side elementary school is under construction at 10125 McGrath Road — 500 new K–5 spaces, estimated occupancy April 2027 — which may redraw east-side catchments.

Strata block, governing no East Chilliwack stock: if a strata lot were ever lawfully produced on non-ALR ground here, the BC block would apply to the LOT — Form B (SPA s. 59); depreciation reports every five years for stratas with five or more lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws void since November 24, 2022; only 55+ age bylaws valid (Strata Property Act ss. 123.1/123.2 and Regulation 7.01, May 1, 2023 exemptions); a "45+" listing line is not a valid age bylaw.

The East Chilliwack listing feed shows Rosedale (Bunker Road) lots, but Rosedale reads as its own community east of the city. A buyer who finds an "East Chilliwack" lot should confirm which community the parcel is actually in before pricing it as East Chilliwack ground.

The tax bill has two extra lines. Chilliwack levies drainage and dyking taxes on top of the municipal rates, so a farm parcel's holding cost is higher than the municipal line alone suggests — and the penalty clock is two-step (5% after July 2, 2026, a further 5% after August 4, 2026).
The new school can move the catchment map. The Province lists the new east-side elementary at 10125 McGrath Road (500 K–5 spaces, estimated occupancy April 2027) as under construction.

blocks.text: East Chilliwack: streets and boundaries

items.t: Its school corridor is Chilliwack Central Road: East Chilliwack Elementary is at 49190 Chilliwack Central Road, per the Province's school list.

The City classifies its neighbourhood plans as urban, hillside and rural; East Chilliwack's farmland falls under the Agricultural Area Plan, Schedule B1 of the 2050 Official Community Plan (OCP), not a standalone neighbourhood plan.

blocks.text: East Chilliwack: the housing stock

items.t: The City states nearly 70% of land in Chilliwack is in the ALR and not available for development, which shapes why East Chilliwack stock stays low-density.

blocks.text: East Chilliwack: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The Agricultural Area Plan, Schedule B1 of OCP Bylaw 2025, No. 5500, is the plan covering East Chilliwack farmland.

Development Permit Area D-4, Farm Home Plate, requires residential buildings on valley-floor farmland to cluster in a farm home plate, leaving the balance for agriculture, where siting does not conform to zoning.

Floodplain Regulation Bylaw 2018, No. 4519 applies: in standard-dike areas habitable floors must meet the flood construction level for the Fraser, Chilliwack and Vedder rivers, plus 0.6 metres freeboard, unless a covenant and qualified professional's report support a waiver.

blocks.text: East Chilliwack: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: East Chilliwack Elementary offers before/after care through Little Valley 123 Child Care, listed on SD33's early-learning site.

Fraser River flood response phases are keyed to the Mission gauge, at about 5.5 metres bankfull and 6.0 metres for minor flooding in unprotected areas, per the City flood information read in earlier work and its Flood Protection page.
Hillside land in Chilliwack is defined by the City for subdivision purposes as land with slopes of 20 percent or more — relevant only at East Chilliwack's upland edges, not the flat farm floor.
Most subdivisions require a tree and green space management plan under Tree Management (Land Development) Bylaw 2008, No. 3585, before final approval.

items.t: SD33's new east-side elementary school, opening September 2027, is the confirmed institutional project on Chilliwack's east side affecting Rosedale and Cheam catchments near East Chilliwack.

items.t: City utility rates are billed quarterly; farm properties may be on well or septic rather than city services — confirm servicing on the Tax and Utility Rates page by address, as no East Chilliwack-specific rate was published there.

blocks.text: East Chilliwack: getting around

items.t: BC Transit route 71 on Yale Road is the nearest listed bus corridor, running downtown Chilliwack to Harrison Hot Springs through Rosedale.
Route 66, Fraser Valley Express, provides the regional Highway 1 bus link from Chilliwack toward Lougheed Station.

items.t: Check the City's floodplain maps and Floodplain Regulation Bylaw 2018, No. 4519 for the specific lot's flood construction level before buying a valley-floor home.
Check ALR status with the ALC and farm home plate siting with the City before planning a second dwelling, suite or non-farm building.

faq.a: School District No. 33 (SD33) transportation lists the Eastern Hillside/East Chilliwack area as East Chilliwack Elementary School, Rosedale Traditional Community School, and Chilliwack Secondary School. That three-school pathway, elementary on Chilliwack Central Road, middle in Rosedale, secondary in Chilliwack Proper, is the pattern a buyer should verify for their exact address.

In May 2026 SD33 approved splitting Cheam Elementary's catchment between Little Mountain, Strathcona and the new east-side elementary opening September 2027, and moving Rosedale Kindergarten-Grade 5 students there. East Chilliwack Elementary was not named in that decision.
